review.headline: A Two Knights where you were comfortably ahead but the clock and 32.Kf1 cost you

sections.text: In the Two Knights Defense you played the aggressive 4.Ng5, and after 5.exd5 Na5 6.Bb5+ Bd7 you tried 7.a4?!. Black took with 7...Bxb5??, and you recaptured with 8.axb5!, a good reply that opened the a-file for your rook (+1.0).

9.Nf3?? gave away much of the advantage, as 9.O-O was cleaner. But 10...Qxe2+? and your recapture 11.Kxe2! was the right way to take back. After 11...e4? you were around +2, with Black's knight stuck on a5, and 14.Rxa5 picked it up.
You played well in the technical middlegame, building from +2 to +4.5 by move 29. 21.d5? and 23.c3? loosened things a little, and 30.Nc6? was a mistake (4.8 to 2.7).
Then time pressure hit. 32.Kf1?? was a blunder that left you at -3.3, but Black replied 32...h5?? and you recovered with 33.Kg2!. The position stayed at +4 or more but you flagged on move 41.

review.turning_point: 32.Kf1?? briefly flipped the evaluation, but even after you recovered at 33.Kg2! the clock decided the game.
review.focus: From move 30 on you were low on time with a winning position. Use simple, safe moves such as 32.Nd4 and keep the king active rather than long knight maneuvers.

review.headline: A Queen's Pawn game where you were doing fine until the Ng5 and Qh5 attack on f7 arrived

sections.text: As Black against 1.d4 you played the Stonewall-like setup of 2...e6, 3...Nf6, 4...Be7 and 5...O-O against White's early 4.f4. 6...Re8?! was a bit odd, but 8...b6 and the position was fine.

9.e4 dxe4 and 10.Nxe4 gave you a decision. 10...Nxe4? let White recapture, and 10...Bb7 was the strongest. 11...Rb8?! then dropped you to -2.2. White returned the favour with 12.Bb1??, and you found 12...Bb7!, the best reply.

Then the attack started. 13.Ng5 aims at f7, and 13...h6?? was the wrong answer; 13...Nf6 held. After 14.Qh5, 14...Nf6?? was a blunder (-5.2): 14...Rf8 defended. 15.Qxf7+ took a pawn with check, 15...Kh8 16.Qg6 and you ran out of time shortly after.

review.turning_point: 13...h6?? and 14...Nf6?? let the queen and knight combine against f7, and the evaluation went from -0.6 to -5.2.
review.focus: At 14...Nf6, count attackers on f7: queen on h5 and knight on g5 against a single defender. 14...Rf8 added defence.

review.headline: A calm Queen's Gambit setup spoiled by 18...g5??

sections.text: This was a Queen's Pawn game where you played a Queen's Gambit Declined setup: 3...Nf6, 4...Be7, 5...O-O and 6...Nbd7. That was fine, and the evaluation stayed within a few tenths of level the whole way.

11...exd5?! was a slight inaccuracy, but the structure was still healthy. 13.Nb5 and 15.Ba3 kept White active, and 16.Bxe7 Qxe7 traded the bishops. 17...Qb4?! was playable but made your queen slightly exposed.

The decisive error was 18...g5??. It opened your king and dropped the evaluation from +0.1 to -2.2; 18...Qd6 was the calm move. After 19.Nxg5 you tried 19...Ne4??, aiming at the queen on d2 and knight on g5 with a fork, but 20.Ngxe4 simply took it and 20...Rxe4?! couldn't repair it.
You played 77% accuracy, so most of the game was good. It's the kind of loss where one impatient pawn move undid ten good ones.

review.turning_point: 18...g5?? loosened the king, and 19.Nxg5 made things worse; 19...Ne4?? lost a piece for nothing.
review.focus: At move 18, you were fine. When there's no clear plan, play a waiting move like 18...Qd6 rather than a pawn push in front of your king.

review.headline: A Philidor where you missed a fork at move 6 and the clock ended a recovering game

sections.text: You played the Hanham setup with 3...Nd7 and recaptured on e5 after 4.dxe5 Nxe5. 5...Bd7?! was a little slow, and White made a serious mistake with 6.Bg5??
That was your moment. 6...Nxf3+ forks the king on e1 and the bishop on g5, with a strong initiative for you in the engine line. Instead 6...Nf6?? let White out, and the evaluation came back to level.

10...O-O-O? was another slip, and then 11.Bxa7? gave you a chance. 11...b6?? was the wrong answer; 11...Nxf3+ 12.gxf3 was better. White replied with 12.Bxb6?? and you found 12...Qxb6!, the best reply, and you were up material. 14...dxe5! was another accurate recapture after 14.Nxe5?.
You played well from move 12, and 17...Bxe2 gave you real material (+4). But 19...Nxe4?? left you with a piece to be won, and you timed out at move 20. 19...Rd4 was the right idea.

review.turning_point: 6.Bg5?? gave you a clear chance with 6...Nxf3+ and a fork on the king and bishop. 6...Nf6?? let it slip away.
review.focus: At move 6, when the opponent leaves a piece loose, look for checks first. 6...Nxf3+ forked king and bishop.

review.headline: An Italian where early mistakes by both sides led to a messy win on time

sections.text: You opened with the main line: 3.Bc4, 4.c3 and 5.d4. Black's 6...Bb6? and 7...d5? gave you the initiative, but 8.e5?? gave it back and 9.Nc3?? put you at -3.5. 9.Bb3 was the right move there.
Credit to you for 10.Nxd5!, a strong reply after 9...f5??, and 11.Nxb6 won a piece. From there you were at +5, with 12.d5 gaining space and the bishop on c4 still strong.

The middlegame got messy. 13.Qd4?! and 15.e6?! were not the cleanest, and 16...Bxf1 took the exchange. 18.Ne5? let Black off: 18.Kxf1 was better. 19...Nf6?? gave it back, and 20.Bg5? missed 20.Kxf1 again.
With little time left, 22.d6?? was a risk, and 22...Qxd6?? left Black worse. 23.Qxf6! finished with a strong position, and Black ran out of time.

review.turning_point: 10.Nxd5! punished 9...f5?? and 11.Nxb6 put you clearly ahead. That's the move to learn from.
review.focus: Look at 9.Nc3: your knight step walked into trouble. 9.Bb3 was simple. Check what the opponent's last move attacks before developing.

review.headline: You were under pressure in a Colle, a good tactic at 18.Qxf4 went unnoticed and time ran out

sections.text: White's Colle setup with 4.Bd3, 5.O-O and 7.c3 was solid, and by 10.e4 and 11.e5 White had the space. You were already at around -1.2. 12...g6?! and 14...f5 were reasonable, but 15...Bxg5?! opened lines for White's bishop.

You were worse, and 16...f4?! (-3.3) hurt, but then White gave you a chance. 18.Qxf4?? took your pawn and put the evaluation at +0.5 for White. The move was 18...Nfxd4, which unmasks your rook on f8 against the queen on f4 as a discovered attack. After 18...Nd6?? you were back at -5.9.

You did find 24...Nxh6!, the best reply to 24.Bxh6?, and 25.Rxf8+? was a chance, but 25...Rxf8? should have been 25...Kxf8. With the clock low, 26.Bxg6?? and 26...Nxg6?? ended the game: 26...Nxg4 was the move, and after 27.Qxg6+ and 28.Qxh6+ you were material down (-3). You flagged shortly after.

review.turning_point: 18.Qxf4?? gave you a real chance, but 18...Nd6?? missed 18...Nfxd4 and the discovered attack on the queen.
review.focus: At move 18, loose-queen tactics: when the opponent's queen lands on f4 in front of your rook, look for a knight move that uncovers the rook. 18...Nfxd4 was the move.

review.headline: A Petrov where 6.Nd5?? gave you a big edge, and you finally won after some shaky moments

sections.text: The game began as a quiet Petrov with 3.d3, 4.Bg5 and 5.Nc3. White then blundered with 6.Nd5??, and you found the best reply, 6...Nxd5!, which won a piece and raised the evaluation to +4.9.
But 7...Qxe7?? let the advantage slip, since 7...Nxe7 8.Qd2 kept the extra piece. After 8.exd5 you were only +1.2, and 8...Bg4 and 9...c6 did not make the position easier.

White's 11.b4? and 12.a3? were mistakes that gave you +1.9 and +1.6, but your 11...a5? and 12...Nb6? let it slip back to +0.1. The better plan was 11...cxd5 12.O-O Be6. After 13.O-O?, your 13...cxd5! got the edge back to +1.2.

White blundered with 16.g3??, and your 16...Nxe2+! brought the evaluation to +8.4. After that you had a huge edge. 29...d3+ and 33...Qf4+ were small slips, and 35...d5?? nearly gave it back, but White answered 36.b5??, and 36...Qxb8! took the queen. White resigned.

review.turning_point: 6...Nxd5! won a piece, but 7...Qxe7?? gave it right back. The later 16...Nxe2+! was the move that made the win straightforward.
review.focus: 7...Qxe7 allowed 8.exd5, which won your knight back. 7...Nxe7 was the safer recapture, so always compare recaptures before choosing one.

review.headline: Black's queen raid worked because 8.Kd2 gave away an advantage that was already yours

sections.text: This was an Exchange French where you opened with 3.d4?! after 2...e6 and Black's queen recaptured on d5. The queen came to f5 and then g4 while you developed with 4.Nc3, 5.Nf3, and 6.Bd3.
7.h3 chased the queen, but it also left g2 undefended, and 7...Qxg2 took a pawn and attacked your rook on h1. The engine actually had you at +4.1 here, because the queen is in danger on g2.

The right reply was 8.Rh2, trapping the queen: 8.Rh2 Qxh2 9.Nxh2 Bd7 10.a3 keeps you comfortably ahead. Instead 8.Kd2?? let the queen escape with 8...Qxf2+, and your king was exposed in the middle of the board. The game was over soon after.

review.turning_point: 8.Kd2?? turned a +4.1 position into -2.5, because 8.Rh2 was the move that made the queen's raid fail.
review.focus: After 7...Qxg2, stop and ask what the greedy queen has left behind. The plan was to attack it with 8.Rh2, not to move the king.

review.headline: A well-played Philidor where you were close to winning, then the clock took over

sections.text: You played the Italian-style setup with 3.Bc4 and 4.d4 against the Philidor. 7.O-O? was a small slip, since 7.Qd5 was a sharper way to pressure b7, but you recovered quickly. 9.Bd2 and 10.b3 were solid and kept the structure sound.

The middlegame belonged to you. Black's 18...Qxc3? allowed 19.Nxc3!, a clean recapture, and the evaluation jumped to about +1.6, growing steadily as you bought pressure with 20.Bg2 and 23.e5. By move 33 you were at +3.4 with your king marching into the centre.

That's what makes the finish painful. From +3.2 at move 41 you were low on time, and 42.g4?? dropped the evaluation to -0.1, with 44.g5?? and 46.Kh7?? repeating the pattern. Black's 42...Ne3?? and 44...hxg5?? gave you chances, and 43.Bd3! was a good reply, but the clock ran out at move 47.
Overall, a quality performance until the very end: 79% accuracy with a structured plan.

review.turning_point: You were +3.2 at move 41, but 42.g4?? was played in time trouble and the advantage was gone; the flag fell later.
review.focus: In the endgame, 42.g4 was a hurried pawn push. When the clock is low, make the safest move (42.Bd3) and keep the king and bishop together.
